headline: Splitting the tab group across modules costs the styled lane one `styled(Tabs)` fold that stays runtime when imported, so `vanilla` edges the css-prop fold here where it trailed it in the single-file `tabs`.

microbench.why: Folding is a same-module rewrite: the tab primitives still fold because their use sites travelled into `parts.tsx` with them, but `FullWidthTabs` is now imported into `index.tsx`, so its `styled(Tabs)` wrapper cannot fold at the foreign call site and stays a runtime `Yak`. The css-prop fold has no `styled(...)` wrapper to lose across the boundary and holds at 0.948 ms/1k; the styled lane carries the extra wrapper at 1.43 ms/1k. `vanilla` (0.821 ms/1k) leads because it hand-writes flat markup with nothing to fold.

autocannon.why: Under load the css-prop fold serves 1.4× the styled lane because its render carries no residual wrapper; both clear the runtime libraries, which re-serialize per request (`emotion` 140 req/s, `panda` 206 req/s).

attribution.why: The css-prop fold's library slice is 0.108 ms; the styled lane's is 0.478 ms — that gap is the imported `FullWidthTabs` wrapper the fold could not reach. `vanilla` renders in 1.15 ms with no styling library at all. The runtime libraries put their cost in the lib slice: `styled-components` 1.64 ms, `emotion` 3.99 ms of their renders.

hydrate.why: Extracted lanes hydrate with zero style/layout/paint; the css-prop lane's flatter tree edges the styled lane. The runtime libraries inject their sheet during hydrate and reflow — `styled-components` and `goober` reach 198 ms and 183 ms, ~3.9× the extracted floor.

inp.why: The static-class lanes update the tab subtree in ~7 ms, inside the interaction spread — a tie. The runtime libraries pay their sheet re-touch: `styled-components` 12.9 ms, `goober` 14.6 ms, `emotion` 25.1 ms.

mount.why: Extracted lanes mount at ~89-95 ms; the runtime libraries add first-inject — `goober` 185 ms, `styled-components` 202 ms, `emotion` 209 ms, ~2× the extracted floor.

renderTiming.why: One style recalc for every approach — parity on paint and layout; the styleMs spread does not order by styling method.

payload.why: Splitting the module does not change the shipped bytes: the css-prop fold stays smallest at 2.39 kB gz, the styled lane 3.46 kB, and the runtime libraries 4.4-6.3× larger (`styled-components` 15.9 kB, `cnfast` 21.9 kB).

nsweep.why: At 4000 groups the styled lane's residual imported wrapper compounds to 64.5 ms, roughly double the css-prop fold and `vanilla` (~30-35 ms). The hash libraries scale by their per-element serialize (`emotion` 193 ms).

crossCase: Reading `multifile-composition` against the single-file `tabs` above isolates the module boundary: the heavy primitives keep folding because their use sites moved with them, and the only casualty is the one `styled(Tabs)` wrapper (`FullWidthTabs`) that becomes an import — worth about 0.04 ms/1k on the styled lane, while the css-prop fold is unaffected. The boundary erodes folding by one wrapper, it does not defeat it.
